Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE...

It would have been a completely different story had Abdullah Shafique held onto the edge of Marsh at first slip when he was on 20. Australia were 16 for 4 at that moment and in a lot of trouble. That would have created a lot of panic and who knows Australia would have been bowled out around 150 but that is not the case. Mitchell Marsh was just not giving up. He and Smith removed Australia from an unwanted position and added around 150 runs. That partnership could be the game-changing one. For Pakistan, Shaheen Afridi and Mir Hamza were brilliant as they ended with four each. Now then! Chasing more than 300 is going to be a tough task. Pakistan need their top four to bloom, one of them has to play a big role. Can they do though against the mighty Aussies?

The Pakistani bowlers have done their job but we feel they have given too many runs in this morning session. The plan was to take the remaining four wickets quickly, Pakistan did but by giving away more than 60 runs. Australia definitely will take this score. Alex Carey had to play a big part this morning. He along with the tail batted well, Cummins and Lyon played a small cameo but it was Carey's 53 which helped Australia get over 310.

Pakistan's fielding was again the thing which let them down! Had they hung onto their chances, they could have well been in the ascendancy over here. However, credit to their bowlers for the way they have bowled. The likes of Mir Hamza and Shaheen Afridi were absolutely brilliant. Both have three each but they will be disappointed with how the rest performed. They would have expected a lot better from the likes of Hasan Ali and Aamer Jamal! Pakistan though will know a couple of wickets early on Day 4 and they are on top in this game. Australia on the other hand, will hope Carey along with the lower-order can take them to over the 300-run mark which won't be an easy chase. The first session on Day 4 will be quite important. What a day of Test cricket! Absolutely brilliant. Have to say, in the end, that wicket of Steven Smith means, the game is quite evenly poised at the moment. However, Australia will be pretty pleased with how they have recovered. They were 16 for 4 at one stage but then it was the Marsh and Smith show. Both joined hands and scored over 150. Marsh was the aggressor whereas Smith played how he usually does. The two bailed Australia out of trouble before Marsh fell. Once he fell, run-scoring was tough. Smith and Carey went along at a very slow pace. Commentary.Commentary: ...Day 3, Session 3...

A session Australia will be really proud of. From 16 for 4, they have come out of the black hole and now lead by 161 runs, all thanks to Mitchell Marsh for the way he played, he took the counterattacking approach. He wasn't shy of hitting it big and with some lady luck has removed Australia from an unwanted position. Steven Smith has played a handy job as well from the other side. Pakistan will be kicking themselves though, they had a chance to get back in this game. They were brilliant with the ball but their fielding was below standard. Marsh was dropped at first slip when he was on 20 and now Pakistan are crying for his wicket. There were too many misfields as well lately. Pakistan need to break this stand quickly or else it won't be easy for them. Australia on the other hand will hope to march on and end the day on a high. Stay tuned.

Pakistan could not have asked for a better start with the ball and it is their talisman, Shaheen Afridi who has delivered. They just had the three overs before the break and Shaheen Afridi has got two big wickets. Australia are effectively 60 for 2 at the moment and will be under pressure after the break. Pakistan on the other hand, will be rearing to go yet again. They will need to keep picking wickets and they will hope Shaheen Afridi can continue his form and the others can give him able support. Australia on the other hand, need a partnership, they will have two of their best batters out there after the break and they will hope they can deliver. Join us for the second session in a bit.
